title: Open restriction and disjoint pullback of native adic extension by zero
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. For any scheme $X$, let $B_X$ be the locally finite continuous $\Omega$-valued coefficient sheaf of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], applied on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ itself rather than on a geometric fibre, and let $\mathcal A(X)=\operatorname{Mod}(B_X)$. Use the same lisse and constructible conditions as that framework: lisse means pro-etale locally $B^{\oplus r}$ with $r$ finite and allowed to depend on the covering member; constructible means locally on the scheme a finite constructible locally closed partition with lisse restrictions. For a scheme morphism $f:Y\to X$, let $f^*M=B_Y\otimes_{f^{-1}B_X}f^{-1}M$, with the coefficient map induced by precomposition of functions. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $j_!:\mathcal A(U)\to\mathcal A(X)$ be sheafification of the extension-by-zero presheaf on the localized ringed site, as specified in [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. For every $M\in\mathcal A(U)$, the adjunction unit is an isomorphism $M\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*j_!M$. For every scheme morphism $g:W\to X$ whose image is disjoint from $j(U)$, the actual module pullback satisfies $g^*j_!M\cong0$. No quasi-compactness hypothesis on $j$ or $g$ is needed.
